evidence: Sen. Vit. Beat. 25.1: quī manum ad stipem porrigunt, those who hold out their hand for alms
Suet. Aug. 91.2: stipem … ēmendīcābat ā populō
M-O s.v. charity: contribution or donation, alms
terms.comment: A small coin given to a beggar, or offered to a god (Lewis & Short); the nominative is not found.

evidence: Vulg. Mt. 6.3: Tē autem faciente eleēmosynam
M-O s.v. charity: contribution or donation, alms
terms.comment: Greek ἐλεημοσύνη, mercy: the word of the Gospels and the Church, also written elēmosyna. To give alms, eleēmosynam facere (Vulg. Mt. 6.2).

phrases.latin: In Sublicium pontem mē trānsfer et inter egentēs abjice: nōn ideō tamen mē dēspiciam quod in illōrum numerō cōnsēderō quī manum ad stipem porrigunt.
phrases.english: Put me on the Sublician bridge and throw me among the needy: I shall not despise myself for sitting among those who hold out their hand for alms.

phrases.latin: Ex nocturnō vīsū etiam stipem quotannīs diē certō ēmendīcābat ā populō cavam manum assēs porrigentibus praebēns.
phrases.english: Because of a dream he even begged alms from the people every year on a fixed day, holding out his cupped hand to those who offered him coins.

phrases.latin: Tē autem faciente eleēmosynam, nesciat sinistra tua quid faciat dextera tua
phrases.english: But when you give alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand is doing
